recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the current-core narrative pointer requested by the seed while preserving extension-pack ownership of the StructureDefinition.
issue_request: FHIR-5872 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU1 change request asking for a standard extension to link OperationOutcome to Contraindication and for the existing OperationOutcome/Contraindication wording to point to that mechanism.
initial_application: Jira says the issue was applied in SVN revision 5862; git commit 361aa07d5c81530bc985e333d2ab7d318c8d09b8 is that revision and added an OperationOutcome.issue extension referencing Contraindication. Later git/Jira history renamed Contraindication to DetectedIssue and updated the OperationOutcome narrative name.
additional_context: FHIR-5259 established the wording that FHIR-5872 augmented. FHIR-8043 renamed Contraindication to DetectedIssue, and source/fhir.ini shows OperationOutcome and DetectedIssue as active resources while recording Contraindication as a retired name. Commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 removed OperationOutcome extension definitions from core, and the FHIR Extension Pack now owns the canonical operationoutcome-detectedIssue definition.
reconciliation: Edited source/operationoutcome/operationoutcome-introduction.xml to link the OperationOutcome/DetectedIssue paragraph to http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/operationoutcome-detectedIssue, without duplicating the extension definition back into core.
source_changes: source/operationoutcome/operationoutcome-introduction.xml: added a canonical link to the OperationOutcome Detected Clinical Issue extension in the Boundaries and Relationships paragraph that describes pairing OperationOutcome with DetectedIssue.

related_jiras.note: Established the OperationOutcome/Contraindication wording that FHIR-5872 was intended to augment with a standard extension mechanism.
Renamed Contraindication to DetectedIssue, which determines the current resource name and extension target profile.
